name: tutorial-interactive
description: Plays the Tutorial Pit the way a first-time player does: every step is driven by a real click on the control the tutorial card points at — speed button, toolbar, hire buttons, blast panel, event choices — and each beat waits for the tutorial's own rails to advance (waitForTutorialStep) before the next click, mirroring the retired playtest definition's click path (seismic survey at 23,23; the box cut dug down the west face before the drill grid; drill grid on the exact 20,20-30,30 rectangle; haul before deliver). Every tutorial-facing step is role-marked 'player' or 'setup' (issue #479): a player step's interaction may not fall back to a console command, so a step that cannot actually be clicked fails the scenario instead of passing on a typed shortcut. #1338: plays on honestly -- real starting cash, no bootstrap skill grants, no campaign complete; free-play sales (any ore_sale or rubble_disposal offer the warehouse already covers, via fillable:true) until the profit target ends the level on its own; with the driver hired before the box cut (#1339) the profit target takes a long run of sales. #1363: the win counts operating profit, so the console clock reaches the target after five sales (steps 47-62); the later sales are interactionOnly because the browser's clock spends more ticks on payroll and needs them, and interaction mode skips them once the level has ended.

steps.description: Setup: load Tutorial Pit with its real starting cash (#1338: no cash: override -- the tutorial is played on the budget a player actually gets, and every purchase below is a real click).

Step hire-surveyor: coach mark docked bottom-centre, Crew button glowing, mine still visible. #904: the tutorial now opens on hiring (completable immediately, no ticks required) instead of time-speed — suggesting a faster clock made no sense as the very first card, with an empty site and nothing queued a faster clock would deliver sooner.

Command-mode-only unpause (issue #585): tutorial_start now genuinely sets isPaused (matches a real player's first view of the tutorial, paused so the card can be read) -- and tickCommand's own loop stops after exactly one real tick while paused regardless of the requested count, so every bare `tick N` below (training waits, haul waits) would silently advance only 1 tick without this. Interaction mode's own waitForTutorialStep steps drive their own real clock independent of console pause state, so this resume has no effect there.
Player follows the glowing Crew button — the tutorial card must not swallow the click

hire-surveyor complete: Hire clicked in the crew panel, surveyor appears on site, card advances straight to Survey Terrain. #923: the speed-control lesson no longer sits here at all -- it moved off this stretch entirely into the box-cut ramp-dig wait further down, so hiring advances directly to 'survey' now instead of by way of a standalone time-speed step.

expect.note: The tutorial is on rails: leaving for the world map mid-step is how a player loses it, so that button must be inert while the tutorial is up (mirrors tutorial.json's hire-surveyor beat).

steps.description: the hired surveyor can actually be sent to survey: opening the Survey panel alone must already show a usable Run button — a surveyor who cannot survey is not a surveyor. If Run is disabled here, hiring grants no geology qualification and no button in the game grants one (mirrors tutorial.json's own standalone beat).

survey complete: seismic (the method the card names), target picked inside the step's outlined region (18..28), dispatched, and the surveyor walks out and works it. waitForTutorialStep drives the real clock for the walk — no scripted `tick` needed once a click starts it.

toggle-survey-overlay (#905): clicking the Survey panel's own overlay-toggle button (#496) clears the confidence quads and the tutorial card advances. Panel is already open from the survey step above.
hire-driller complete: driller hired through the crew panel

#1041: tutorial rails allow navigating to ANY panel, not just the active stage's own target. The rail is still pointing at the Build toolbar button (stage 'build-living-quarters'), but the Fleet toolbar button is a [data-panel] control belonging to no stage at all -- before #1041 it was blocked exactly like a state-changing action, sealing the player behind whichever panel a stage happened to target. Opening it here must genuinely work, and must not move the tutorial off 'build-living-quarters' -- looking around is not progress.

expect.note: PANEL_OPEN_SELECTOR ([data-panel], tutorialStepHelpers.ts) is baked into BASE_PERMANENTLY_ALLOWED (tutorialRails.ts) so every panel opener stays clickable regardless of the active stage.

steps.description: #1041 (cont.): closes the Fleet panel just opened, via its own header close control -- also permanently allowed, independent of the active stage. Confirms the panel genuinely closes (not merely that the click didn't throw) and that the tutorial is still sitting on 'build-living-quarters', unmoved by the detour.

expect.note: PANEL_CLOSE_SELECTOR ([data-panel-close], PanelBase.ts) is the close-side half of the same permanent allowance -- stamped on panelHeader()'s close button so every panel built through it (Fleet included) can be dismissed without a per-panel rails entry.

steps.description: #681: build-living-quarters, click half -- the tutorial's new step 3a-i, placed right after hiring the driller and before the box-cut/drill-plan/charge stretch that used to run this crew unmanaged for ~400 ticks. A tier-1 living_quarters gives that stretch's forced rest somewhere real to send a collapsing employee. #556: ordering a building queues a construction site instead of placing it instantly -- this step only confirms the order landed (orderedBuildingCount increases); the wait step right below drives the site to completion the same way drill-plan/charge below it wait for holeCount/chargedCount. #1008 follow-up: moved off (18,18), whose footprint included (20,20) -- the exact grid cell a fatigue-interrupted employee near the drill grid can freeze at (clampToGrid, Pathfinding.ts), permanently stranding them once a building occupied it. #1008-followup (PR #1023): (12,15), while flat, still deadlocked this exact step in real interaction-mode CI -- its footprint sat only 2-4 tiles from the vehicle spawn point (16,16) and the box-cut corridor (x:16, z:19-31), the same freeze radius as (18,18)/(20,20) above, just measured against different danger points. Moved to (6,16) -- flat, 10 tiles clear of every hazard -- but a second real interaction-mode run showed (6,16) deadlocks box-cut too, a fatigue/rest round-trip livelock rather than a stranding: the round trip is so long the excavator's fatigue crosses back over the rest threshold before a single ramp segment carves. (29,12) cleared every hazard by >=5 tiles while roughly halving the round trip -- see tutorialStages.ts's own REGION.livingQuarters comment for the full trace. #1040: moved again to (29,11), alongside driving_center (29,14) and freight_warehouse (25,12), so the three pins form one stated, checkable compact cluster (TUTORIAL_SITE_CLUSTER_MAX_SPAN_TILES/TUTORIAL_SITE_DIG_ROUND_TRIP_MAX_TILES, balance.ts) instead of each being justified by its own one-off stranding postmortem. #1170 follow-up: the slope-based navmesh (#1151) made a real walking route far longer than the straight-line tile bound the cluster used to be measured against, so the whole cluster moved west of the box-cut corridor to living_quarters (8,15), driving_center (6,15), freight_warehouse (8,18) -- this step's own `command`/`pickTile` fields already target (8,15); the bound is now checked against real pathfinding route cost, renamed `TUTORIAL_SITE_DIG_ROUND_TRIP_MAX_ROUTE_COST` (balance.ts) -- see tutorialStages.ts's own REGION doc comment for the full trace.

#1014: once the living-quarters order lands, the buy button's own click is spent -- the tutorial card must stop re-instructing a control the player has already used and show the waiting state instead: the stage line swaps to the construction-underway sentence, the WAITING chip becomes visible, and the rails release the buy button's highlight while it stays genuinely clickable (still bs-tutorial-allowed, not abandoned). Observes only -- the building has not landed yet at this point (orderedBuildingCount still holds the pending order); the wait_until step right below still owns driving buildingCount to completion. Issue #1014: this step's own timeout (60s) wraps its whole chained interaction array (3x waits at 15000ms each, worst case 45s) -- raised past that worst case rather than split, matching level2-playthrough-win.json step-96/98.

interaction.expectedValue: Order placed — waiting for the crew to finish building it.

steps.description: #556/#816: build-living-quarters complete -- the driller or surveyor (both idle, no skill required for place_building) walks to (8,15) and builds the tier-1 living_quarters over its ~40-tick base duration. Waits on buildingCount itself rather than waitForTutorialStep, matching the drill-plan/charge waits below -- the tutorial card only flips to 'set-early-policy' once the building genuinely exists. #1170: pin moved west of the box-cut corridor alongside driving_center (6,15) and freight_warehouse (8,18) -- see tutorialStages.ts's own REGION doc comment for the full trace.

#681: set-early-policy complete -- the tutorial's new step 3a-ii. A living_quarters alone does not force anyone to rest: forceShiftRestIfNeededByPolicy (GameLoop.ts) only engages once state.sitePolicy.revision > 0, so this policy application is what actually makes the building above protect the crew through the grind that follows. Selects Continuous under Shift schedule first, then Apply -- shift_8h's own SHIFT_DURATIONS_TICKS (8) is shorter than a single drill_hole action, so applying it this early interrupted the queued vehicle-gated work below before it could finish (confirmed live pre-#700). Continuous still forces rest on hunger/fatigue (shouldForceRest checks that in every mode), just without the shift-length cap. The later set-policy step (unchanged) still teaches shift_8h once the grind is over. #707: timeout 15 -> 30 -- this was the only step in the file below the 30s floor every other player step uses; its `waitForTutorialStep` action's own inner deadline defaults to 30000ms (interaction-executor.ts) but effectiveStepTimeoutMs (scenario-utils.ts) doesn't know that action's `timeout` field (only `timeoutMs`/its own DEFAULT_INNER_TIMEOUT_MS table), so the outer 15000ms raced and lost first on a slow (no-GPU, #475) render -- confirmed live: the tutorial card had already reached 'build-driving-center' by the time the step's own 15s wall clock expired. #1151: the rest threshold is now set explicitly to 75 instead of left at its default 60 — the same change e11081b made to the identical step in tutorial-steps-visual.json, for the same reason: under the 30-degree slope gate a drive to a drill hole is long enough that a worker protected from rest-interruption mid-drive arrives with almost nothing left. e11081b measured that in command mode, where only the sibling file showed it; this file fails the same way in interaction mode only, where the extra real ticks a player-driven step spends deepen the same drain. Measured here: wellBeing falls 99.99 -> 1.34 across the nine-hole drill wait and the run ends in a worker revolt at the zone-clear step. Resting at 75 starts the walk back while it is still affordable. #1338: threshold 75 -> 65. Resting in place restores only to NEED_REST_NO_BUILDING_CAP (70), so any threshold at or above 70 makes an idle crew far from living quarters re-trigger rest forever once their fatigue sits at the cap; with real starting cash (no grants to outrun the payroll) that stall bankrupts the run. 65 still rests the crew before the grind drains wellbeing but can always be left.

hire-driver complete: driver hired through the crew panel. #776: raised from 30s to 60s -- same shape as the hire-manager and the retired accept step (#1335) steps' own #776 fixes above: effectiveStepTimeoutMs's formula-correct ~35000ms (30s declared vs innerMs+margin) proved empirically insufficient in two independent interaction-mode runs, both timing out here with the real hire + tutorial advance to vehicle-buy-assign already having succeeded before the deadline fired. #776 follow-up: raised again to 90s -- floored with every other post-blast step to this file's own established 90s precedent (steps 31/39/41/42), covering this scenario's shots:["overview","birdseye"] render cost rather than retuning each step by hand. #816: no longer downstream of the set_policy mode:continuous construction livelock -- driving_center/freight_warehouse both complete for real and cash recovers on schedule now that place_building's root-cause livelock is fixed, so this succeeds genuinely. Opens the Crew panel with ensurePanel rather than a bare toolbar click (#556/#817): with the retired accept step (#1335) moved below build-storage, the step before this one is the manager hire and the panel is already open — the toolbar tab toggles, so a second click would close it, and the rail (which lights the last reachable control) makes that click inert.

buy-drill-rig-assign complete (#921): a vehicle's driver is claimed automatically now (VehicleReservation/ArrivalGate) -- there is no Assign click and no `vehicle driver` command left to issue, so the purchase itself is the whole step. Vehicles panel open, tier-1 drill_rig bought and placed on the terrain surface; the tutorial rail advances straight to 'train-digger' on the purchase alone -- the newly-licensed driller (employee #2) boards it on their own once drill-plan below queues vehicle-gated work, with no further player input.

buy-rock-digger-assign complete (#921): same retarget as buy-drill-rig-assign above -- a vehicle's driver is claimed automatically now, so the purchase alone is the whole step. Vehicles panel open, tier-1 rock_digger bought and placed on the terrain surface; the tutorial rail advances straight to 'box-cut' on the purchase alone -- the newly-licensed digger (employee #1) boards it on their own once box-cut's dig_ramp_segment work queues below, with no further player input.

box-cut complete: dig the starter cut down the west face of the drill pattern before the first shot, so the blasted rock has a free face and a void to fall into (real open pits pioneer this access cut first). #923 had advanced the card to 'speed-up-for-dig' next; #1015 removes that step (and its 'speed-normal-after-dig' pair) entirely -- the speed bar is unconditionally player-controlled from the tutorial's first step onward, so box-cut now advances straight to 'drill-plan', same as before #923. #1151: depth explicit 8 -> 6 -- length 12 (z:19-31, can't extend further without running off this 32-wide map's edge) now caps the legal depth at floor(12 / 1.8) = 6 to keep every per-column step within NAV_MAX_SLOPE_RATIO. Flagging for the implementer/CI to verify against a live run: this file's own drill_plan below is depth:8, and Ramp.ts's per-column floor() staircase already undershoots its own nominal targetDepth by up to 1 (the old depth:8/length:12 pairing actually bottomed out at floor(11/12*8)=7, not 8) -- at depth:6 the ramp's real floor is floor(11/12*6)=5, up to 3m short of this file's 8-deep crater floor. A gap that size is illegal under NAV_MAX_SLOPE_RATIO regardless of how ramp length/depth are tuned in this file alone; closing it needs Ramp.ts's own carving to move from a floored integer staircase to a continuous per-column depth (see the identical note in tests/integration/navmesh.integration.test.ts) -- not something a scenario-def edit can fix on its own.

expect.note: Open pits start with an access cut dug before the first shot: blasted rock swells and needs a void to fall into (mirrors tutorial.json's box-cut beat).

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:3 cols:3 spacing:4 depth:8 start:22,20
steps.description: drill-plan, click half: grid tool dragged over the 22,20-30,28 rectangle the card asks for, confirmed. #553: this only orders the 9 holes -- drill_hole became a queued, vehicle-gated action, so holeCount stays 0 until the driller (equipped above) actually drives the drill_rig to each one. The wait is its own step right below. #554-followup (issue #586 CI, rounds 4-5): round 4 corrected the command from rows:3 cols:3 spacing:5 (9 holes) to rows:4 cols:4 spacing:3 (16 holes), reasoning the spacing stepper is unreachable this early in the rail (confirmed live, still true) so the declared spacing:5 could never be real. That was half right: spacing really is stuck at the tool's own DEFAULT_SPACING_M=3, but the drag rectangle producing 16 holes at that spacing was itself a latent bug in the region the tutorial rail snaps this drag to (REGION.drill, tutorialStages.ts), sized for a spacing of 5 that Drill.ts has never actually used since #479 -- nothing caught it because charging was instant until #553/#554, so the extra holes never cost real time. Round 5 fixes REGION.drill directly (20-30 -> 20-26), restoring the tutorial's originally-intended 3x3/9-hole workload for a lone early-tutorial employee with no living quarters yet; a 16-hole grid drove that same employee into a full worker revolt partway through charging (see the charging step's own note below). Command and drag corrected back in step to match the fixed region. #949: spacing/depth/start retuned again, from 3/6/(20,20) to 4/8/(22,20) -- mirrors tutorialSteps.ts's own 'drill-plan' stage retune, which fixes the tutorial's scripted plan so it rates good-or-better instead of catastrophic (verified live against the real engine to rate PERFECT with zero casualties/destruction). `dragTiles` moved to (22,20)-(30,28) to match. #949-followup: added the spacing (3->4, one increment click) and depth (6->8, two increment clicks) stepper clicks before the drag, plus tightened `expect` from `increased: [orderedHoleCount]` to an exact `equals` -- both steppers live on the shared ParamStrip (#bs-param-strip-bar, ParamStrip.ts), reachable the instant the grid tool arms, but were unreachable in this step before tutorialStages.ts's own 'drill-plan' stage allowlisted them (defect 2 fix, tutorialStages.ts). Without these clicks the drag alone produced a 4x4/spacing:3/depth:6 grid at the panel's own defaults, and the old loose `increased` expectation passed on that wrong result by coincidence. This file's own downstream tick/cash figures against the new 4/8/(22,20) plan were verified: command-mode run (`npx tsx scripts/run-all-scenarios.ts tutorial-playthrough tutorial-steps-visual tutorial-interactive`) passes with 0 failures, and interaction-mode run (real Puppeteer clicks, screenshots) passes end-to-end. #1330: superseded by the panel-default retune -- the panel's own defaults are now exactly this plan (grid spacing 4 m, depth 8 m; charge amount 4 kg, stemming 2.5 m), so this step carries no spacing/depth/amount/stemming setStepper actions and any stepper-click wording above is historical.

#553: drill-plan complete: the driller drives the drill_rig to all 9 ordered holes and drills them (sandbox-measured: a single driller/drill_rig lands a 3x3 spacing:3 grid on tutorial_pit comfortably inside 400 ticks door-to-door). #554-followup round 6 (issue #586 CI): previously used waitForTutorialStep(stepId:'charge'), which resolves the instant the FIRST hole lands (createComparisonStep's isComplete fires on the first increase past its snapshot -- 'drill-plan' advances to 'charge' after hole 1 of 9, not all 9). The very next step's `charge hole:*` order then only covered whatever was drilled AT THAT MOMENT -- usually just the one hole -- leaving the other 8 permanently uncharged (no later step re-issues the order), which is what left 'Auto Sequence' unreachable further down: charging never actually finished. Switched to waitUntil on holeCount itself so this step keeps waiting until every hole is actually down, in both modes, rather than stopping the moment the tutorial card first flips.

Defensive: a `tick N` step silently completes fewer ticks than requested if a random event fires mid-wait, and every subsequent tick then refuses until the event is resolved. No-op when nothing is pending.

charge ordered: Charge All Holes clicked — the panel applies its own form defaults and hole rows turn amber/loading (#554: charging is real work now, so the click only queues the order; the wait step right after drains it and confirms the tutorial advances to sequence once every hole has actually landed). #949: standardized on boomite (matching tutorial-playthrough.json/tutorial-steps-visual.json, and the panel's own DEFAULT_EXPLOSIVE, Charge.ts) -- the old pop_rock/3kg/2m command never actually matched what a real click produced anyway (Charge All always applies the panel's own boomite/5kg/2m defaults, a pre-existing command/click divergence this file carried before #949), so no explosive-selector click is needed. Amount/stemming steppers now clicked explicitly to reach the retuned amount:4/stemming: the amount stepper's step is 1kg (5->4, one decrement click) and the stemming stepper's step is 0.2m (2.0->2.2->2.5, two increment clicks) -- 2.5m is the closest reachable value to the 2.5 this step first declared (the command now declares 2.5 too, so both channels run the same value -- setStepper refuses a target the control cannot reach), and functionally equivalent to it: both sit at or above BlastCalc's own full-stemming-effectiveness cap of 0.3x depth (0.3*8=2.5m at this pattern's depth:8), so the extra 0.1m the console command asks for does nothing more. The stepper click count/selectors were verified against a real interaction-mode run (Puppeteer, screenshots). #1330: superseded by the panel-default retune -- the panel's own defaults are now exactly this plan (grid spacing 4 m, depth 8 m; charge amount 4 kg, stemming 2.5 m), so this step carries no spacing/depth/amount/stemming setStepper actions and any stepper-click wording above is historical.

#554-followup round 6 (issue #586 CI): earlier rounds waited only for the FIRST charge to land (tutorialStep flips to 'sequence' the instant chargedCount first increases -- createComparisonStep's isComplete, same premature-advance behaviour as drill-plan above) and moved on with 8 of 9 holes still uncharged. That left 'Auto Sequence' unreachable further down the file: the sequence panel's own auto-sequence control only ever became reachable once every ordered charge had actually landed, so a scenario that stopped at chargedCount:1 could never proceed no matter how the following steps were reshuffled. Waiting for full completion here (chargedCount:9) is the real fix -- the drill-plan step above now also waits for all 9 holes before charging is ordered (round 6), so this order only ever targets the full 9 in the first place, unlike the partial orders earlier rounds were chasing. A 16-hole grid at this same lone-employee, no-living-quarters stage drove a full WORKER REVOLT at cumulative tick 318 (WorkerRevolt.ts's REVOLT_TICKS=120 sticky-zero window); REGION.drill (tutorialStages.ts) was fixed at the source to restore the tutorial's originally-intended 3x3/9-hole workload, which comfortably finishes charging well short of that threshold.
#1362: FIRE then DETONATE once. DETONATE sounds the horn itself and fires automatically as soon as nobody is left in the danger zone -- no separate Sound the Horn, wait, FIRE sequence.
#1362: wait for the automatic fire -- the blast clears the plan (holeCount 0) only once the evacuation finished and the sequence fired.

blast complete: Execute clicked, confirm dialog answered, crater and fragments appear, Blast Report closed; the scores card then waits for the player (#1334: no auto-dismiss) (#1362: the blast already fired by itself; this step closes its report.)

expect.note: Close dismisses BlastReportModal, which auto-opens with the real report right after DETONATE; scores card waits for a player action (#1334), so the next beat inspects the scores HUD (mirrors tutorial.json's own choice not to assert it here). holeCount/chargedCount resetting to 0 is checkable in both modes and goes beyond what the DOM-only playtest reference could prove.

steps.description: #1339: build-driving-center, click half -- ordered after the first blast, which leaves oversized boulders only a rock fragmenter can break; the Driving Center teaches its licence. Every role arrives able to do its own job, so the old drill-rig and excavator courses are gone.
#556/#816: build-driving-center complete -- the site finishes construction before the fragmenter course is booked.
#1339: train-fragmenter, click half -- the hired Driver (found by role in the crew panel) is booked on the Rock Fragmenter licence at the driving_center.

#1339: train-fragmenter complete -- the course finishes and the driver holds driving.rock_fragmenter. waitForTutorialStep drives the real clock in interaction mode; command mode needs the explicit tick.

#1334: scores card does not auto-dismiss. The player inspects the scores HUD with a real click on #bs-hud-scores (pointerenter/click raise its inspectCount); only that action completes the card, after which the scripted consultant event fires. Waits on the tutorial reaching the next card, not on a delay.

event-fire-resolve rail restriction (#951): the stage highlights only the first (`event choose 0`, +$15 well-being for -$3,000) of the consultant event's 3 choices, whose effects differ materially -- so the 2nd option (`event choose 1`: -10 well-being/-5 safety) must be genuinely inert while the dialog is open, not merely un-highlighted. Proven as unreachable (`expect.blocked`, interaction mode only) rather than clicked -- a real click that cannot land is exactly what a guard step exists to prove, per checkStepActionAllowed's own contract. Command is a harmless `state` read: this step performs no player action of its own, only a proof, so command mode has nothing to assert here.

expect.note: the un-highlighted -10 well-being/-5 safety option must stay inert so a player cannot pick it by mistake instead of the highlighted +15 well-being option

steps.description: event-fire-resolve rail restriction (#951), 3rd option: same proof as the preceding step for the event's other un-highlighted choice (`event choose 2`: +5 well-being/-5 safety) -- both siblings of the highlighted first choice must be inert, not just one.

expect.note: the un-highlighted +5 well-being/-5 safety option must also stay inert

steps.description: event-fire-resolve complete: the consultant dialog is answered through its own buttons, outcome read, then dismissed. Click is scoped to `:first-child` (#951) -- the tutorial stage's own target, and the only choice the two guard steps above leave reachable. #776: raised to 90s -- this and the following post-blast steps (blast at step 31 leaves a 994-fragment muck pile this scenario never fully clears) each pay for this file's own shots:["overview","birdseye"] (2 screenshot renders + a state dump) under software-rasterization cost; step 37 below already failed on shot-capture cost alone with its actual command succeeding, so raised to the file's own established 90s precedent (steps 31/39/41/42) rather than retuning each step individually.

hire-manager complete: manager hired now that the event is resolved. #776: raised from 30s to 60s -- this step lands right after the blast sequence (steps 24-31) when the scene is heaviest, and effectiveStepTimeoutMs's formula-correct 35000ms (30s declared vs innerMs+margin) proved empirically insufficient in two independent interaction-mode runs, both timing out at exactly 35000ms with the real hire + tutorial advance to the retired accept step (#1335) already having succeeded before the deadline fired. #776 follow-up: raised again to 90s -- floored with every other post-blast step to this file's own established 90s precedent (steps 31/39/41/42), covering this scenario's shots:["overview","birdseye"] render cost rather than retuning each step by hand. Card sequence follows tutorialSteps.ts’s reordered canonical order (#556/#817): the retired accept step (#1335) now sits after build-storage, so a contract’s deadline no longer starts while a construction site is still going up.

#816 retarget: the two new order-then-wait pairs inserted upstream of the blast (build-living-quarters/build-driving-center, #556 construction sites) push this step's own command-mode entry tick from 303 to 621 (direct trace, command mode, this fix) -- roughly the +250-300 real ticks those two waits themselves cost, on top of #816's own root-cause dispatch fix (relocating a bystander stranded on a just-completed building's footprint, and letting an idle employee fall through to the open pool when its own taskQueue holds one permanently-unreachable entry) actually letting driving_center/drilling/charging complete for real instead of livelocking forever. Direct-traced (command mode) that a rubble_disposal offer is continuously present in the pool from tick 622 through at least tick 1021 (400-tick scan) -- unlike the earlier #689/#707 rounds' narrower single-instance windows, every ~20-tick rotation in this range still carries a rubble_disposal slot, so this step no longer needs to land inside one specific instance's narrow window. Retargeted 420 -> 721 (100 ticks above the command-mode floor of 621) with max_ticks widened 140 -> 220 to also clear a materially larger interaction-mode entry tick than command mode's own 621 -- interaction mode's extra role:'player' polling ticks (waitForTutorialStep/waitForSelector loops command mode's plain `command` string never runs) were already ~100 ticks ahead of command mode at a similar point in earlier, shorter rounds of this file (#707 follow-up 2's own tick-370-vs-303 trace), and this file has grown since; not independently confirmed under a live interaction-mode run this round (no browser session in this fix pass) -- if interaction mode's own entry to this step is ever traced past 721, retarget upward the same way #689/#707/#707-followup-2 each did, using the continuous-presence property above rather than re-deriving a narrow window. REPLACED for #556: an absolute tickCount target cannot hold here — command mode and interaction mode enter this step hundreds of ticks apart (interaction mode runs polling ticks command mode never does), and `equals` only matches going forward, so any single number is either already behind one mode or out of reach of the other. What the step actually needs is in the note above: a rubble_disposal offer is continuously present through this range, not confined to one narrow window, so a short relative block that turns the pool once (REFRESH_INTERVAL 20 ticks, Contract.ts) buys it in either mode. #1015: 30 -> 40 -- removing the two speed-control steps (and their ~658-tick box-cut-drain wait) upstream shifts every later tick landing earlier by a similar amount, changing which rubble_disposal pool instance the later the retired accept step (#1335) step lands on; direct-traced (command mode) against the retimed run, `tick 30` here now lands the retired accept step (#1335) on an instance whose deadline the haul can't beat regardless of how the delivery-side wait is tuned (deadlineTicks 31, hauler load lands 37 ticks after accept). `tick 40` lands on a different instance (deadlineTicks 58, hauler loaded 9 ticks after accept) with real margin either side -- see the haul-debris step's own #1015 note below for the matching delivery-side retune.

vehicle-buy-assign complete (#921): the purchase is the whole step now — a vehicle's driver is claimed automatically (VehicleReservation/ArrivalGate), so there is no Assign click and no `vehicle driver` command left to issue. Vehicles panel open, tier-1 hauler bought and placed on the terrain surface; the tutorial rail advances straight to 'build-storage' on the purchase alone. The driver hired and licensed above (employee #4) boards it on their own once haul-debris queues vehicle-gated work further down, with no further player input — the #478 deadlock path is exercised through the automatic claim path instead of a manual Assign click. #776: raised to 90s -- post-blast step under this scenario's shots:["overview","birdseye"] render cost; floored to the file's own established 90s precedent (steps 31/39/41/42) alongside its neighbors rather than retuning individually. #816: no longer downstream of the set_policy mode:continuous construction livelock -- cash recovers on schedule now that place_building's root-cause livelock is fixed, so this succeeds genuinely.

#1042 CI-fix: replaced the fixed `tick 200` + eight `tick 20` pad that stood here with the same `wait_until fillableOreSaleOffered` pattern #1048 already proved for this exact fragility in tutorial-steps-visual.json. #1042's evacuate-zone fix (a qualified employee now genuinely drives a driverless vehicle clear instead of the horn stranding it unconditionally) shifts every tick this file's own trajectory lands on downstream of Sound the Horn -- direct-traced (interaction mode, this fix): tickCount 680 after this step used to require `tick 200` alone to reach 771, and the old fixed pad of eight further `tick 20` calls (aimed at tick 832, where dirtite offer #47 was confirmed present under the pre-#1042 timing) instead rotated a fillable offer that was already on the board at 680 back out by 821 -- `fillableOreSaleOffered` read true at 680 and false again at 821, which is exactly the shape of failure #1048's own history describes: a fixed pad aimed at one pool instance breaks the moment anything upstream re-times the run into a different one. `fillableOreSaleOffered` (console-api.ts) waits on the real condition -- the pool holding an ore_sale asking no more of its ore than the site already has -- rather than a tick count guessed against one trajectory, so it holds regardless of how many ticks evacuate-zone or any future upstream change spends. Dropped the `material:dirtite` pin on the two steps below for the same reason: this pit's two blasts only ever produce dirtite in fillable quantity (every other offer this file's own history sees -- absurdium/rustite/craktonite/blingite -- is never actually held in storage), so a generic fillable match resolves to dirtite in practice without re-pinning the scenario to one pool composition an upstream retime can roll away from under it, same as #1048's own fix. #1091-followup: max_ticks 400 -> 4200 (timeoutMs 120000 -> 600000) -- #1090's dispatch-cost reordering changes the absolute tick this run's RNG stream rolls a fillable ore_sale offer on (same condition, different draw sequence; see the new_game step's own #1091-followup note on the matching cash bump this required). Direct-traced (command mode) the match now lands 3798 ticks into this wait (tickCount 4300), not within the old 400-tick budget. 4200 keeps ~400 ticks of margin above that measured landing point, the same margin-over-measured-landing philosophy every earlier retune of this exact step already used. #1131 CI-fix: max_ticks 4200 -> 60000 -- the #1091-followup retune above was measured in command mode only, and CI's shard 5/10 (interaction mode) stalled at max_ticks:4200 as a result. Direct-traced (interaction mode, real browser, this fix, same PR): this run's own RNG stream lands the match at tickCount 14100, 13634 ticks into this wait (it starts at tick 466) -- over 3x command mode's own 3798-tick landing, and well past the old 4200-tick budget. 60000 keeps ~46000 ticks of margin above that measured interaction-mode landing point; wall-clock cost of the extra ticks is cheap (this whole 53-step scenario, end to end, ran in well under 400s in this fix's own verification run) so the ceiling is set generously rather than tightly retuned, matching this file's own #1015/#1091 precedent of paying real margin over the measured landing rather than the minimum that clears it. Re-verified command mode at the same max_ticks: still lands at tickCount 4300 (3798 ticks in), unaffected -- raising the ceiling doesn't change where a mode's own RNG stream resolves, only how much headroom is left above it. See the new_game step's own #1131 CI-fix note for the matching cash bump this required (2,000,000 -> 50,000,000) to keep interaction mode's much longer wait solvent.

#959, the issue's own missing half, first beat: Accept clicked on an ore_sale offer this pit can actually fill -- rock its own blasts produced and its own haulers carried in. #1042 CI-fix: scoped to `[data-contract-type="ore_sale"][data-contract-fillable="true"]` rather than to `material:dirtite` -- which ore the board asks for is random per refresh (Contract.ts's generateContracts), so naming one pins this step to a pool composition that any upstream re-timing (like #1042's own evacuate-zone fix) re-rolls, same failure #1048 already fixed this same way in tutorial-steps-visual.json. `data-contract-fillable` is the card's own `stored >= quantityKg`, the same figure its "have" bar already colors green, and the DOM counterpart of the `fillableOreSaleOffered` the preceding step waits on. A `waitForSelector` ahead of the click gives the refresh cycle time to surface the right card rather than assuming it's there instantly. `commandOutcome: 'either'` is command-mode only: the two modes' tick trajectories diverge well upstream of here (this file's haul-debris step waits on the tutorial rail in interaction mode and on a fixed `tick 22` in command mode), so the same wait_until above lands command mode on a different offer pool, where the console can refuse this accept outright. The sell beat is proven by the click path, in interaction mode, which is the mode that models a player at all.

steps.description: #959, the issue's own missing half, second beat: Deliver clicked on the accepted contract, and with it the tutorial finally turns blasted ore into money. Nothing is typed into the amount field: ContractsPanel pre-fills it with `min(remaining, stored)` (`maxDeliverable`), so a plain click delivers exactly what storage can cover, which is the mechanic the 'sell-ore' card's own text teaches. #1042 CI-fix: click scoped to `[data-contract-type="ore_sale"]` alone (no `material:dirtite` pin, same reasoning as the accept step above) -- safe unscoped-by-material here because the accept step already narrowed the pool to exactly one active contract, the same way tutorial-steps-visual.json's own sibling step does it. `commandOutcome: 'either'` for the same command-mode trajectory reason as the accept step. Reaching 'set-policy' rather than 'sell-ore''s immediate successor is deliberate: 'finances' and 'needs' after it are auto-advance cards that move on by themselves after a fixed beat, so whichever is showing when this step's goal is evaluated would be a race -- 'set-policy' is the next card that waits for a click and therefore stays put once reached. Before #959 this beat did not exist at all: the tutorial hauled its muck pile to storage and then walked past it to the closing card.
